caveat: Digests cover predictor code, not model weights: the weights are synced to the worker from weights_source at run time and are not present in this process. A matching digest therefore means the same scoring code, not provably the same weights.

model_card.feature_cols: see feature_columns.json (300 features, top-300 of ~1490 raw descriptors selected by XGBoost gain importance)

feature_sources.aaindex1_protscale: 19 curated AAindex1 accessions (mean/std/min/max per sequence, 76 dims) standing in for classic ExPASy ProtScale tables; values bundled in aaindex1_scales.json, extracted from the source project's aaindex1 database file
feature_sources.biopython: Bio.SeqUtils.ProtParam.ProteinAnalysis global descriptors (19 dims: MW, aromaticity, instability index, GRAVY, pI, charge at pH7, secondary-structure fractions, molar extinction, compositional fractions)
feature_sources.propy3_pybiomed: propy.PyPro.GetProDes: amino-acid composition, dipeptide composition, CTD, Moran/Geary/Moreau-Broto autocorrelation, QSO, SOCN, PAAC, APAAC (~1275 dims; QSO/SOCN/PAAC/APAAC lag=4)

model_card.target_description: Aggregation propensity label (seed_bh) from adt5111_data_files_s1_to_s7.xlsx, sheet SD_2.

model_card.caveat: Severe class imbalance (23/206 positive) and small n drive low MCC/Recall for both deployed models despite class-weighting. Treat angiogenic_dominant as a soft screening signal, not a high-confidence classifier.
model_card.deployment_object_provenance: Each of the 2 deployed models (SVM, MLP) was fit ONCE on the FULL 206-row dataset (fit_production_model in pipeline_35M_embedder.ipynb, no held-out fold) -- the notebook's own designated deployable object, distinct from the per-fold models fit during LOOCV which exist only to produce honest out-of-sample metrics. A RandomForestClassifier was also fit but is not part of the deployed ensemble. Exported from 'Models/Angiogenic activity prediction/pipeline_35M_embedder.ipynb' (despite the filename, this run embeds with facebook/esm2_t30_150M_UR50D).
model_card.ensemble_architecture: 2 independently trained models (a 3rd, RandomForestClassifier, was trained in the source notebook but excluded from the deployed ensemble), each a Pipeline wrapping a ColumnTransformer([passthrough 16 physchem descriptors, StandardScaler->PCA(0.95 variance) over 640-dim ESM2 block]): SVC(probability=True) and a custom TorchMLPClassifier (3-layer MLP). Deployed prediction is the unweighted mean of the two models' P(angiogenic_dominant).
model_card.esm_pooling: mean-pool per-residue hidden states, excluding BOS/EOS
model_card.evaluation_metrics_source: notebook's own per-fold Leave-One-Out CV (206 folds), NOT a direct evaluation of the deployed full-data-refit objects -- reported as the best available generalization estimate since the deployed objects have no held-out evaluation of their own

feature_computation.boman_index: negated mean Boman (1995) side-chain transfer free energy; higher = more protein-binding potential
feature_computation.cysteine_fraction: fraction of residues equal to C
feature_computation.glycine_fraction: fraction of residues equal to G
feature_computation.hydrophobic_fraction: fraction of residues with positive Kyte-Doolittle value
feature_computation.hydrophobic_moment: Eisenberg hydrophobic moment assuming alpha-helix, 100 deg/residue, normalized by sequence length
feature_computation.net_charge: Henderson-Hasselbalch net charge at pH 7.0 using side-chain pKa (K 10.5, R 12.5, H 6.0, D 3.9, E 4.1, C 8.3, Y 10.1) plus N-term pKa 9.0 and C-term pKa 2.0
feature_computation.proline_fraction: fraction of residues equal to P

mlp.loss: NLLLoss over log(softmax) output, class weights [1, 5]

hyperparameters.note: class_weight/pos_class_weight of 5 reflects heavy class imbalance (23 positive / 183 negative in training data)

training_data.cleaning_filter: Sequences non-null, fullmatch [ACDEFGHIKLMNPQRSTVWY]+, deduplicated by sequence; label = 'Angiogenesis ' column cast to int

model_card.architecture: UniZyme joint model (UniZyme\SE structure-only ablation): shared EnzymeEncoder + ActiveSiteHead produce a pooled enzyme representation h^e; SubstrateEncoder produces per-residue substrate hidden states H^s; CleavageSiteHead gathers a +/-15-residue window of H^s around each candidate position, concatenates with h^e, and scores a per-residue logit via MLP. See architecture.py and README.md.
model_card.caveat: The cleavage task's training set is small (52 enzymes) relative to the active-site task's; the joint loss (loss_c + 10*loss_a) leans on the active-site task to shape the shared enzyme encoder. Treat cleavage-site probabilities as a screening signal for protease susceptibility, not a validated high-confidence prediction -- especially for enzyme accessions far from the training distribution (non-human orthologs, unusual families).
model_card.checkpoint_provenance: unizyme model/joint_model/best_model.pt from the source project, retrained end-to-end on facebook/esm2_t30_150M_UR50D embeddings (enzyme PCA refit to 640-dim input; supersedes the earlier 35M-embedder epoch-13 checkpoint). Selected during training by lowest val_combined_loss, epoch 8. Model_state_dict, epoch, and best_score are as saved by the source checkpoint.

checkpoint_val_metrics_epoch8.note: From the source checkpoint's own training-time history (epochs 0-8); this 150M-embedder retrain's best epoch differs from the prior 35M-embedder export's epoch-13 checkpoint (val_pr_auc_cleavage 0.8298) -- the two are not directly comparable runs. No independent held-out evaluation was re-run for this update -- these are the source project's own validation-split metrics, not a fresh test-set score.

model_card.enzyme_panel_selection: Curated from the source project's aligned+verified enzyme manifest (8,921 of 9,807 candidate UniProt EC 3.4 entries) by matching protein_name/enzyme_id against wound-healing-relevant protease families: matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs)/collagenases/gelatinases/stromelysins, cathepsins, elastases, plasminogen activators. Not the full manifest -- the full manifest is genome-wide EC 3.4 proteases (~1.1GB embeddings alone) and mostly irrelevant to wound biology.
model_card.enzyme_side_backbone: facebook/esm2_t30_150M_UR50D, PCA-reduced to 128 dims by enzymes/pca_model.joblib (IncrementalPCA fit on the source project's enzyme train split -- reused unmodified, not refit here)

inference_inputs_required.distance_matrix: (len(sequence), len(sequence)) float array, pairwise C-alpha Euclidean distance in Angstroms, from a resolved or predicted 3D structure of the candidate peptide -- NOT computed by this predictor, must be supplied by the caller
inference_inputs_required.enzyme_accession: UniProt accession of a bundled enzyme (see enzymes/enzyme_catalog.csv), or omit to score against the full 118-enzyme panel via predict()
inference_inputs_required.sequence: candidate peptide amino-acid sequence, standard 20 AAs

model_card.known_coverage_gap: Human MMP-1 (P03956), MMP-2 (P08253), MMP-3 (P08254), MMP-8 (P22894), MMP-9 (P14780), MMP-12 (P39900), and human neutrophil elastase (P08246) are NOT in the bundled panel -- their structures failed the source pipeline's aligned+verified check (structure length did not match sequence length) and were dropped upstream, before this migration. The panel does include their non-human orthologs (rat/mouse/rabbit MMPs, mouse neutrophil elastase Q3UP87) and a handful of human family members (MMP-11, MMP-19, MMP-24, MMP-26, ELA1_HUMAN, EL2A_HUMAN). Treat cleavage-site predictions against non-human orthologs as directional evidence of protease-family susceptibility, not a substitute for the specific human enzyme.
model_card.substrate_side_backbone: facebook/esm2_t30_150M_UR50D, same pca_model.joblib transform applied (pca_model.transform(...), not a separately fit model)
model_card.task: Per-residue P1 protease cleavage-site probability for a candidate peptide (substrate), against a bundled panel of enzymes (proteases).
model_card.training_data_scale: ~7,844 UniProt-labeled enzymes (active-site task), ~52 aligned enzymes with MEROPS cleavage data (cleavage task) -- see source MODEL_ARCHITECTURE.md section 3.4 for why only 52 enzymes have usable cleavage training data despite the much larger active-site set.

model_card.cv_protocol: 10-fold KFold(shuffle=True, random_state=42) over the full 147-row dataset; species_ohe, both StandardScalers, and PCA refit inside each fold on that fold's training rows only
model_card.esm_embedding: mean-pooled last_hidden_state, excludes BOS token and final valid (EOS) token, sequence uppercased before tokenization
model_card.final_fit: both physchem/esm2 preprocessing, the SVR, and the RandomForestRegressor are refit on all 147 rows (not just the 115-row train split) before saving
model_card.model_selection_note: RF and SVR are statistically indistinguishable under 10-fold CV. Both are deployed as an unweighted-mean ensemble to combine their independent error profiles, rather than picking one.
model_card.model_type: ensemble: SVR (kernel=rbf, C=10.0, epsilon=0.1, gamma=scale) + RandomForestRegressor (n_estimators=300, max_depth=None, min_samples_leaf=2, random_state=42), unweighted mean of the two predictions

physchem_notes.amphipathicity: custom, not native modlAMP: hydrophobic_moment / mean(abs(eisenberg per-residue H))
physchem_notes.d_residue_fraction: fraction of lowercase residues in raw sequence (D-amino acid marker), sequences folded to uppercase for all other descriptors

preprocessing_order: 1. compute 14 modlAMP physchem descriptors on the raw sequence
3. compute ESM2-150M mean-pooled embedding (640-dim) on the uppercased sequence
5. esm2_pca.transform (PCA fit on scaled training embeddings, n_components=0.95 -> 27 PCs)
7. concatenate [species_onehot, physchem_scaled, esm2_pcs] -> 54-dim vector -> SVR.predict and RandomForestRegressor.predict, averaged
model_card.species_ohe_handle_unknown: ignore (out-of-vocabulary species map to an all-zero one-hot vector, not an error)
model_card.train_test_split_for_cv_reference: 115 train / 32 test, stratified by species with a floor of 1 per split (final models are refit on all 147 rows)

model_card.ensemble_method: simple unweighted mean of BiLSTM, CNN, and Random Forest predictions (not computed by the source notebook; combined here per export instructions)
model_card.esm_embedding_type: per-residue (last_hidden_state), BOS/EOS dropped, left-aligned into a fixed MAX_SEQ_LEN=50 slot with zero padding

components.DNC: dinucleotide composition, 16 dims (all AA..TT pairs, normalized frequency)
components.NAC: mononucleotide composition, 4 dims (A, C, G, T frequency)
components.TNC: trinucleotide composition, 64 dims (all AAA..TTT triplets, normalized frequency)

genome_feature_scheme.name: NAC + DNC + TNC genomic nucleotide composition
genome_feature_scheme.source: precomputed once per organism from genome FASTA files in the source project's genomes/ directory; stored as genome_vectors.json in this package (no FASTA files shipped)

model_card.loss_function: weighted MSE loss used to train BiLSTM and CNN; censored rows (MIC reported as '<' or '>' a bound) down-weighted to 0.5x vs 1.0x for uncensored rows -- NOT bound-aware (does not enforce the prediction stay on the correct side of the bound), simply reduces the influence of uncertain targets

bilstm.architecture: BiLSTM(esm_dim=640, hidden=128, bidirectional) over per-residue ESM2 embeddings (packed by true residue length) concatenated with a GenomicANN(84->64->32) branch over the genome vector, BatchNorm, then a 2-layer MLP regressor (288->64->1)
bilstm.training: AdamW lr=1e-3 wd=1e-4, batch=64, up to 150 epochs, early stopping patience=20 on val weighted-MSE loss (censored rows downweighted 0.5x), best checkpoint restored

cnn.architecture: Conv1D(640->128,k=5)+ReLU+MaxPool2, Conv1D(128->64,k=5)+ReLU+MaxPool2 over per-residue ESM2 embeddings (padded positions zeroed pre-conv), flattened, concatenated with the same GenomicANN(84->64->32) branch, BatchNorm, then a 2-layer MLP regressor (800->64->1)
cnn.training: AdamW lr=1e-3 wd=1e-4, batch=64, up to 100 epochs, early stopping patience=10 on val weighted-MSE loss (censored rows downweighted 0.5x), best checkpoint restored

random_forest.feature_composition: 319 iFeature protein descriptors + 84 genome NAC/DNC/TNC features

ifeature_descriptor_set.CTDC: 39 dims, composition/transition/distribution - composition (13 physicochemical properties x 3 groups)
ifeature_descriptor_set.CTDD: 195 dims, CTD - distribution (13 properties x 3 groups x 5 percentile cutoffs)
ifeature_descriptor_set.CTDT: 39 dims, CTD - transition (13 properties x 3 transitions)
ifeature_descriptor_set.PAAC: 20 dims (Xc1, amino acid composition term) + 1 dim (Xc2, lambda=1 sequence-order term), pseudo amino acid composition with lambda=1 (source project peptides too short for the PAAC default lambda=30)
ifeature_descriptor_set.vendored_from: iFeature (Chen et al., https://github.com/Superzchen/iFeature), reimplemented in predictor.py so no external iFeature install is needed at inference time; numerically validated against the original iFeature codebase output on multiple test sequences (exact match)

random_forest.training: fit directly on point-estimate log10_mic_um target (no censored-loss variant for RF; all rows, including censored ones, trained on their point estimate)

model_card.task: regression: log10(MIC, uM) for a peptide against one of 3 ATCC reference organisms

training_data.restricted_to: 3 ATCC reference organisms only (Escherichia coli, Staphylococcus aureus, Pseudomonas aeruginosa)
training_data.sources: CAMP + DRAMP + DBAASP, combined and deduplicated with CAMP > DBAASP > DRAMP priority
training_data.split: 75/12.5/12.5 train/val/test by CD-HIT 90%-identity cluster (whole clusters assigned to one split, greedy balance of split size + per-split species mix)

model_card.deployment_object_provenance: FULL-DATA REFIT for deployment. Notebook (pipeline.ipynb) never persists a fitted model: build_ensemble() is built fresh inside every Leave-One-Out CV fold, fit on that fold only, used once, then discarded; no joblib.dump/pickle exists in the notebook. The two .joblib artifacts shipped here were fit once each on the FULL 103-row dataset (no LOO holdout) using the exact same feature code and hyperparameters as the notebook, by a standalone script outside the source project, per explicit user authorization. This is a deliberate deviation from the notebook's own protocol (training-set size only: full data vs n-1 rows per LOO fold).
model_card.ensemble_architecture: VotingClassifier(voting='soft') over RandomForestClassifier + XGBClassifier + Pipeline(StandardScaler -> LogisticRegression), one independent ensemble instance per target
model_card.evaluation_metrics_source: notebook's own per-fold Leave-One-Out CV (103 folds per target), NOT a direct evaluation of this deployed full-data-refit object -- reported as the best available generalization estimate since the deployed object has no held-out evaluation of its own

deployment_artifact.split_strategy: pair_stratified: random 64/16/20 train/val/test split stratified on y (peptide-solvent pairs can appear across both train and test)
deployment_artifact.variant: Pipeline B raw (ESM2 embedding + solvent descriptors, no PCA)
deployment_artifact.why_chosen: pipelineB.ipynb was read in full and contains no full-data refit step after the evaluation loop (the notebook ends at the LOSO summary in the final cell). All 6 cached B_raw artifacts are evaluation-fold models: pair_stratified and seq_disjoint each hold out a test partition, and the 4 loso_* files each hold out one entire solvent. There is no cached or in-notebook model trained on 100% of long_peptide_solvent.csv. Per the documented fallback rule, pair_stratified was selected as the most defensible deployment choice: it uses the largest train portion, is a standard random split (not group-held-out), and is closest in spirit to a general-purpose model. This is a FALLBACK, not an ideal full-data-refit deployment model — see README.md Provenance section.
